notes: Scene 8 plays on the shared farm places in the lamp-niche frame; only the west gate square has its own grid, in the city of Kallias's court.
The montage is two plans and four beats joined by hard cuts, the wheat under the harvest sun and then three rain-dark dusks at the gate lamp and the fold.
The first rain and the winter beat open on the same frame of the gatepost, so the seasons turn at the same lamp.
In the city the last sun comes level through the west gate, so the traveller sees the garland and the stained hem in the only light in the square while the street lamps come on to the east.
The traveller comes on the last day of the wheat harvest, so the gate by day, the lamp at dusk and the fold at night are one day and one evening.

At the gate by day the camera works from the road in the wall's shade, so the trough, the gateway and Amos on the bench share one line of sight and Eliab appears in the sunlit gateway behind the talkers.
At dusk Eliab keeps his face to the road through every line and turns only at the end; the camera reads his face from the road and takes Amos's place in the gateway for Esau's running.
At the fold the camera stays inside among the sheep, so both men's faces come over the wall in the light of Amos's lamp, with the kid between the camera and Amos.
Amos leaves the dusk and the night the same way, walking away inside the yard while his father stays at a lamp.
W30 is chosen stillness, the camera low in the straw through the whole long look at the kid, and the dusk take ends in a slow pull-back down the road.
